findings.location: scripts/i06_backend_profile_v4.py check_vectors (section counts and the closing 'unique vector identifiers' check)
findings.finding: check_vectors pins each section's count and each case's result, but not which cases a section holds. In one probe I moved SN01 into crossVersion as a base-v4 case, dropped XR01, and added a copy of SN02 as SN99 to keep the counts. That edited vector was ACCEPTED (132 checks). XR01, the case where I06 v4 refuses v3's own snapshot positive, can therefore be lost without notice, and any meaningful case can be swapped for a trivial one. The uniqueness check covers only v4's own sections: renaming SN01 to S06, a v3 snapshot case id that v4 replays, was also ACCEPTED.
findings.requiredChange: Pin the case set in the model: the ids of each section, in order, and the shape of the two anchor cases (XR01 on base v3 with no ops, XR02 on base v4 with no ops). Require v4's ids to be disjoint from the replayed v3 snapshot ids. Add the probe to the generator's self-tests.

findings.location: README.md 'Consumers' (HE-004-I01) and 'The exact pin'; the model's module docstring; criteria RB06
findings.finding: Q-RBAC-3 (a) reads: 'Any other binding naming the observer ... makes the observer refuse its snapshot.' v4 splits the pin into two independent functions. check_rbac_snapshot covers RB05. check_observer_rbac covers RB01-RB04 and RB06 over the live lists. Nothing composes them, and no caller obligation says the snapshot is refused when check_observer_rbac refuses. Nor does any obligation require the two checks to judge the same RBAC lists, read at one resourceVersion, that produced the snapshot. The README says only that HE-004-I01 'adds RB05 to the snapshot check and runs RB01-RB04 and RB06 over the RBAC lists it already reads'. A port could therefore run RB06 as a warning, or on a different read, and still match the contract text. ON48, a role holding only non-resource URLs bound to the observer, shows why this matters: only RB06 sees it.
findings.requiredChange: State a caller obligation in the README, the model docstring and RB06's requirement text. The observer accepts its snapshot only if check_rbac_snapshot accepts it and check_observer_rbac accepts the RBAC lists the snapshot was produced from. Alternatively, add a composed function, for example check_observer_snapshot(snapshot, objects, closure, inventory, bootstrap, namespace), and pin it in the vectors.

findings.location: README.md 'Stock group grants', 'Who is the observer', the RB05 and RB06 rows and 'Not claimed'; status.json carried
findings.finding: The certificate makes the observer a member of system:authenticated whatever its O. Any non-stock binding to that group therefore widens the observer, and both checks accept it. My probes: a ClusterRoleBinding of Group system:authenticated to a role holding nonResourceURLs ['*'] was ACCEPTED by check_observer_rbac. So was one to a role with get and list on secrets. The same group gaining get secrets at CLUSTER was ACCEPTED by check_rbac_snapshot, because reads are none of I06's policy-relevant categories. Q-RBAC-7 (a) limits the claim to 'the observer's own bindings', and the README carries the *stock* system:authenticated grants to T04. Non-stock grants to the observer's implicit group are neither 'own bindings' nor 'stock', and no item carries them. The RB06 row justifies leaving Group subjects out with 'the certificate has no O', which does not apply to system:authenticated. RB05 says 'nothing else at any scope', which a reader can take to mean the observer's effective authority.
findings.requiredChange: Say plainly in the RB06 row, 'Who is the observer' and 'Not claimed' that only bindings naming User planeon:policy-observer are pinned. Grants that reach it through system:authenticated beyond the stock bootstrap ones are neither pinned here nor checked by I06 when they are reads. Carry that residual to a named owner, T04 and/or HE-004-I01, in status.json carried. If the monitor prefers, ask whether RB06 should also refuse non-stock bindings to system:authenticated (see the question in this record's checks).

findings.finding: Frozen inputs and the RB rows' text are pinned only through vectors.json's own `inputs` digests, so any edit that also updates those digests passes. My probes, with the pin updated: one I06 v3 snapshot negative replaced by a different consistent case was ACCEPTED; I07 v3's K22 payload edited together with ON45 was ACCEPTED; RB03's requirement or source text edited in criteria.json was ACCEPTED. Without the pin update each was refused. vectors.json is itself sha256-pinned by edge v8, so this is a hardening point, the same pattern as I06 v3 and native-profile v5.
findings.requiredChange: Optional: embed the digests of the frozen inputs (v3 vectors 4752b648..., v3 criteria 752533c5..., I07 v3 vectors c4c24c5f..., writer inventory, closure, bootstrap) and the RB00-RB06 rows (or their digest) as model constants, and assert them in check_vectors.

findings.location: README.md 'The exact pin', 'Why a successor', 'Still open' and 'Consumers'
findings.finding: Wording. (a) 'R10's producer drops every subject's non-resource rules but the loopback user's (rbac.rs:7)': for the loopback user R10 refuses to produce the snapshot (rbac.rs:4-6) rather than keeping the rules. (b) 'v3 accepts the observer with any read added or removed: get or every verb on secrets ...': every verb is not a read; the accurate claim is that v3 accepts any non-policy-relevant grant. (c) 'Still open: v3's list ... carried unchanged' also carries v3's item about the edge-v5 providerPacket TBD, which v3's adoption (MET-ENFORCE-033) discharged. (d) 'labels, annotations ..., ownerReferences and finalizers are refused (ON26-ON28, ON38)': no case holds finalizers. The model refuses them (my probe: 'RB03 ... metadata holds finalizers'). (e) observer-rbac.json residuals[0].ruleIndex is 0-based while the prose and the RB02 refusals number rules from 1. (f) The HE-008 bullet names check_observer_rbac only, while Q-RBAC-4 (a)'s option text has HE-008 check RB00-RB04, which includes the document check.
findings.requiredChange: (a) Say 'drops other subjects' non-resource rules and refuses one bound to the loopback user'. (b) Say 'any grant outside I06's policy-relevant categories'. (c) Carry v3's list 'less OBS-RBAC-1's naming and the discharged edge-v5 item'. (d) Add a finalizers case, or drop the word from the citation. (e) Say that ruleIndex is 0-based (rule 1). (f) Add RB00 (check_observer_document on the vendored document) to HE-008's checks.

checks.check: The role against R10, derived independently from R10's source at 1a0c529 (read as text)
checks.result: PASS. Request is built only in requests.rs: 7 struct literals in 7 builders (list, discovery_group, discovery_version, version, readyz, metrics, progress). A git grep of the observer crate's src finds no other constructor. http::render, called once (client.rs:453), writes 'GET <target> HTTP/1.1' and nothing else (http.rs:55-58). The observe.rs call sites are 656, 680, 757, 764, 810, 847, 867, 986, 1134, 1135 and 1136. Resource::ALL has 20 specs covering exactly the 19 (group, resource) pairs of rules 1-7 (OR05's two share core secrets), all cluster-wide with no label selector. Fresh, Exact and Probe are list; Watch is watch. The fixed targets are /apis/admissionregistration.k8s.io and /apis/admissionregistration.k8s.io/<v> (v validated as [a-z0-9]{1,63}, at most 16), /version, /readyz/poststarthook/rbac/bootstrap-roles, /metrics, and /api/v1/namespaces?limit=1 (list namespaces). The derived set is 19 pairs × {list, watch} plus 5 URLs × get = 43 grants in 8 rules. It equals OBSERVER_RULES; every request is covered and every grant is used. R10's observer_grants() (c_support/mod.rs:369-386, with the b1_rbac_support helpers) equals the contract rule for rule and in order, with the same names and the subject apiGroup rbac.authorization.k8s.io. R10's producer (rbac.rs:242-250) emits a subject's rules in binding then rule order, so RB05's in-order comparison matches what R10 produces for one binding. The /apis/admissionregistration.k8s.io/* pattern is sound: under the apiserver's request-info rules, /apis/<group>/<version> is a non-resource path and anything deeper is a resource request, and stock system:discovery already grants /apis/*. /version under API discovery follows R116 and the stock system:discovery grouping.
